issues.legal_issue: A restricted interest granted to a female Hindu under a will that takes effect after the succession-law reform does not enlarge into absolute ownership merely because she possesses the property.
material_facts: A Hindu male executed a will granting each of his two wives a life interest in one half of his property and making his daughter the ultimate beneficiary.
The testator died after the succession-law reform had taken effect, and the will then operated in favour of the wives.
One wife later made a will purporting to bequeath her interest to a person outside the family.
The courts below treated the wife’s life interest as enlarged into absolute ownership, while the High Court held that she received only the interest specified in the testator’s will.
issues.conclusion: The wife acquired only the life interest granted by the will; it did not enlarge into an absolute estate, and she could not transfer an absolute interest by her own will. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 30 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 recognises a Hindu’s power to dispose of property by will. Section 14(1), including its explanation, broadly enlarges qualifying property held by a female Hindu into full ownership, but Section 14(2) excludes property acquired under a will that prescribes a restricted estate. The exception must be read so it does not defeat Section 14(1), but a restricted estate created by a will that operates after the Act is within Section 14(2); the pre-existing-right reasoning in V. Tulasamma v. Shesha Reddy does not convert such a testamentary grant into an absolute estate. The Court also relied on G. Appaswami Chettiar v. R. Sarangapani Chettiar and Kothi Satyanarayana v. Galla Sithayya concerning restricted interests created by testamentary or other instruments.

rule.if: appeal_concerning_willed_property and will_operated_after_reform and will_granted_lifetime_interest and female_possession_derived_from_will

predicates.appeal_concerning_willed_property: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the nature of a woman’s interest in property received under a will.
predicates.will_operated_after_reform: The testator died, and the will took effect, after a succession-law reform had taken effect.
predicates.will_granted_lifetime_interest: The testator’s will limited the woman’s interest in the property to her lifetime.
predicates.female_possession_derived_from_will: The woman’s possession of the property came from the will rather than from an independently established basis.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns property possessed by a woman under a will that took effect after the succession-law reform and granted her only a lifetime interest, that interest remains restricted.
